title: Dexter stops Lovett using brushes
summary: Lovett was made to play sticks only on record since brushes' 'shish' interfered; Smith defends brush work.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Well, he stopped me from using brushes while we were recording.
He -- (inaudible) -- "shish","shish", that's what he's hearing now, you see, and it interferes with the recording so I had to use sticks all the way.
Yeah but now you know you hear some

beautiful brush work when you hear -- like Georgie Whetling Berigan's on "I Can't Get behind Bunny Burg on the solo and it kind of got started in what, 1936, '37. I would hate to have had sticks on that, you know, to listen to, to my ear, some of the stuff Shelly Manne's done with those brushes and Krupa with that small group, you know, "The Wire Brush Stomp".
Well maybe Dave Dexter -- you know, I'm sure he knew what he was doing.
Maybe the records were a little different.
